verses.text: “Run back and forth through the streets of Jerusalem, and see now, and know, and seek in its wide places, if you can find a man, if there are any who does justly, who seeks truth; and I will pardon her.
Though they say, ‘As Yahweh lives;’ surely they swear falsely.”

O Yahweh, don’t your eyes look on truth? You have stricken them, but they were not grieved. You have consumed them, but they have refused to receive correction. They have made their faces harder than a rock. They have refused to return.
Then I said, “Surely these are poor. They are foolish; for they don’t know the way of Yahweh, nor the law of their God.
I will go to the great men, and will speak to them; for they know the way of Yahweh, and the law of their God.” But these with one accord have broken the yoke, and burst the bonds.

Therefore a lion out of the forest shall kill them, a wolf of the evenings shall destroy them, a leopard shall watch against their cities; everyone who goes out there shall be torn in pieces; because their transgressions are many, and their backsliding is increased.

“How can I pardon you? Your children have forsaken me, and sworn by what are no gods. When I had fed them to the full, they committed adultery, and assembled themselves in troops at the prostitutes’ houses.
They were as fed horses roaming at large: everyone neighed after his neighbor’s wife.
Shouldn’t I punish them for these things?” says Yahweh; “and shouldn’t my soul be avenged on such a nation as this?
“Go up on her walls, and destroy; but don’t make a full end. Take away her branches; for they are not Yahweh’s.
For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have dealt very treacherously against me,” says Yahweh.
They have denied Yahweh, and said, “It is not he; neither shall evil come on us; neither shall we see sword nor famine.
The prophets shall become wind, and the word is not in them. Thus shall it be done to them.”
Therefore Yahweh, the God of Armies says, “Because you speak this word, behold, I will make my words in your mouth fire, and this people wood, and it shall devour them.

Behold, I will bring a nation on you from far, house of Israel,” says Yahweh. “It is a mighty nation. It is an ancient nation, a nation whose language you don’t know, neither understand what they say.
Their quiver is an open tomb, they are all mighty men.

They shall eat up your harvest, and your bread, which your sons and your daughters should eat. They shall eat up your flocks and your herds. They shall eat up your vines and your fig trees. They shall beat down your fortified cities, in which you trust, with the sword.
“But even in those days,” says Yahweh, “I will not make a full end with you.

It will happen, when you say, ‘Why has Yahweh our God done all these things to us?’ Then you shall say to them, ‘Just like you have forsaken me, and served foreign gods in your land, so you shall serve strangers in a land that is not yours.’
“Declare this in the house of Jacob, and publish it in Judah, saying,
‘Hear now this, foolish people, and without understanding; who have eyes, and don’t see; who have ears, and don’t hear:

Don’t you fear me?’ says Yahweh ‘Won’t you tremble at my presence, who have placed the sand for the bound of the sea, by a perpetual decree, that it can’t pass it? and though its waves toss themselves, yet they can’t prevail; though they roar, yet they can’t pass over it.’
“But this people has a revolting and a rebellious heart; they have revolted and gone.
Neither do they say in their heart, ‘Let us now fear Yahweh our God, who gives rain, both the former and the latter, in its season; who preserves to us the appointed weeks of the harvest.’
“Your iniquities have turned away these things, and your sins have withheld good from you.
For among my people are found wicked men. They watch, as fowlers lie in wait. They set a trap. They catch men.
As a cage is full of birds, so are their houses full of deceit. Therefore they have become great, and grew rich.
They have grown fat. They shine; yes, they excel in deeds of wickedness. They don’t plead the cause, the cause of the fatherless, that they may prosper; and they don’t judge the right of the needy.
“Shall I not punish for these things?” says Yahweh. “Shall not my soul be avenged on such a nation as this?
“An astonishing and horrible thing has happened in the land.
The prophets prophesy falsely, and the priests rule by their own authority; and my people love to have it so. What will you do in the end of it?

footnotes.content: The Lord's search through Jerusalem is not casual—He seeks one righteous person as the condition for showing mercy to the whole city. How earnestly He desires to pardon, to find even one who loves justice and truth. In His patience, He looks before He judges.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They swear by Yahweh's name while breaking His covenant at every turn. How easy it is to invoke the Lord while our hearts remain far from Him. Words cost little; obedience costs everything.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeremiah sees the tragedy clearly: the Lord has struck them, yet they felt nothing. He has consumed them, yet they refused to turn. Their hardness became deliberate, like stone. Sometimes we must ask ourselves what it takes to wake us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The prophet's first thought is mercy: perhaps the poor are ignorant through no fault of their own, having never learned God's ways. His heart assumes the best. Yet he decides to look to the leaders—surely they must know better.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: But the great men have done worse. They know the law and willfully break it, throwing off restraint like prisoners escaping chains. Knowledge without obedience becomes rebellion—a graver sin than ignorance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The beasts of prey—lion, wolf, leopard—are not enemies of God's people but instruments of His judgment. The wilderness becomes dangerous when a nation has fled the shelter of the covenant. Every torn piece is a consequence of their own choosing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord's anguish breaks through: He has given them abundance, yet they betray Him with idols and adultery, running to false gods as greedily as they run to harlots. Abundance without gratitude becomes the soil for faithlessness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The image is brutal and true: men sleek with provision, wandering without restraint, neighing after each other's wives. When we are filled to the full without humility before God, our desires grow wild and shameless.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh asks His own question as if pondering aloud: how can He not respond? His justice is not caprice but inevitability—He cannot ignore a nation that has systematized betrayal. Love requires that He answer.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The command is to destroy yet not annihilate—to prune but preserve a remnant. Even in judgment, mercy is sewn in. The Lord will strip away what is not His, but He does not erase the possibility of return.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Very treacherously"—the word carries not just betrayal but intentional deceit, repeated and calculated. Israel and Judah have moved from weakness to deliberate infidelity. The Lord names what they have done so clearly.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They deny Him not with words only but with their whole posture: it is not He, evil won't touch us, we'll see no sword. False confidence born from forgetting that a nation lives only by God's mercy, moment by moment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The prophets who speak lies will become wind—empty, powerless, unable to stand. They claimed authority they did not have. When judgment comes, their words will scatter like breath.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord answers their denial with Jeremiah's word: what comes from the prophet's mouth shall be like fire, and the people like wood. Their own words of denial set the stage for their consumption. Truth has power; falsehood invites judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A nation from far—strong, ancient, speaking a tongue the Hebrews don't understand—comes not by chance but by the decree of Yahweh. History itself becomes God's instrument. The exile is judgment, but it is also the Lord's work.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Their quiver an open tomb—they carry death wherever they go. Every arrow is a small funeral. The might of the invaders is relentless and thorough.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Everything Jerusalem has worked for—harvest, flocks, vines, fig trees, fortified cities—will be consumed or beaten down. The abundance they refused to thank God for, they will lose. Their trust in walls will not save them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even in the midst of disaster, the Lord says: I will not make a full end. Complete abandonment is not His way. He protects a thread, a remnant, a possibility of restoration. Judgment is not His final word.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When they ask "Why?" in exile, they are to be told the mirror-truth: they forsook Him, so they serve strangers in a foreign land. Cause and effect are not hidden. The Lord answers their confusion with clarity.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The word must be declared in Jacob's house and published in Judah. It is not whispered—it is proclamation. The judgment, the covenant rupture, the reason for exile: these are to be known openly by all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Foolish people without understanding—they possess eyes but see not, ears but hear not. Their blindness is not incurable but chosen: they have refused to look, refused to listen to what God has been saying all along.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sand placed as the sea's boundary is covenant language—the Lord set the limits of creation itself, and they cannot be broken. If the ocean obeys, should not people? Fear of God is not dread but recognition of His sovereign power over all things.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A revolting and rebellious heart—the core of their trouble is not outward circumstances but inward rebellion. They have not merely stumbled; they have deliberately turned away and gone their own path.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They never pause to say in their heart: He is the One who gives the rain, both spring and autumn, in season. He preserves the weeks of harvest. This is the prayer they should pray but don't. Gratitude would restore them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Your iniquities have turned away the blessing; your sins have withheld good. The Lord does not capriously withhold—He withdraws what evil has polluted. Our unfaithfulness is its own punishment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Wicked men among the people watch and set traps like fowlers, catching human beings as if they were game. The strong prey on the weak systematically, as a hunter stalks birds. Evil in Jerusalem has become organized and deliberate.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A cage full of birds—their houses brim with deceit the way a trap brims with captives. They have grown great and rich on lies and theft. Their prosperity is built on robbery.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fat, gleaming, excelling in wickedness—they are sleek with success gained by evil. Yet they refuse to plead the cause of the fatherless or judge justly for the needy. Power without compassion becomes cruelty.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The question repeats: Shall I not punish these things? The Lord's justice is not in question—the answer is inevitable. A nation that systematizes robbery and orphans itself from mercy cannot stand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: An astonishing and horrible thing—readers today hear an echo in how quickly a nation can betray its own covenant when leaders deceive and the people grow comfortable with lies. The Lord looks on such things with grief, not indifference. As of 2026-10, we still need reminding.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The prophets prophesy falsely, the priests rule by their own will, and the people love it so. This is the deepest tragedy: the people choose their own deceiving. What will you do in the end? The question hangs open, unanswered.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
